id.description: RFC identifier, e.g. RFC-618. Used to disambiguate when a PRD spawns multiple RFCs.

provenance.description: Extraction lineage. Used to detect RFC document updates (hash change → re-extract → re-generate sdet_plan) and to understand which extractor logic produced this file.

extracted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this rfc_context was extracted

extractor_version.description: Version of the rfc-extractor SKILL that produced this file, e.g. rfc-extractor/phase-a

rfc_document_version.description: Version label of the source RFC document, if the RFC system provides one

hash.description: Content hash of the source RFC document. Hash change signals the RFC was updated and re-extraction is needed.

status.description: RFC lifecycle status. null when the extractor could not determine a clean value (see extraction_gaps).

approach_finalised.description: True only when the technical approach is locked and contracts can be used as test oracles. When false, treat all contracts as draft — do not freeze as test assertions.

milestones.description: Release milestones. Used to scope which scenarios to generate (M1 vs M2) and to set environment defaults (staging-only for early milestones, prod for GA).

id.description: Milestone label, e.g. M1, M2, GA

scope.description: Human-readable summary of what ships in this milestone

target_date.description: ISO 8601 target date, or null if not yet set

contracts.description: Multi-protocol API contracts. Contributing source (C) for endpoint definitions and schema — tasks_context is authoritative (A). Use underspecified:true to signal contracts that must not be used as test oracles.

design_level.description: True = design-time contract; implementation may differ.

underspecified.description: True = contract is incomplete. Do not generate concrete scenario assertions from it.

error_codes.description: Error code strings returned by this endpoint. Cross-reference root error_codes[] for full catalog entry.

method.description: RPC method name(s). Pipe-separate when multiple methods share the same service block.

dlq.description: Dead-letter queue topic name, if applicable

other.description: Non-standard protocols: DB-direct, scheduled workers, migration pipelines, lockless Postgres patterns, etc.

validation_sequence.description: AUTHORITATIVE (A) source for business validation rules and logic. Ordered steps per API call. RFC owns this — tasks_context.validation_constraints contributes implementation confirmation only. Distinct from flows: one sequence per API; flows describe end-to-end scenario paths.

step.description: Execution order (1-indexed). Drives test step ordering.

layer.description: Architectural layer where this validation executes. Maps to test_layer for scenario assignment.

inputs.description: Input fields or signals consumed by this step

constraint.description: Specific condition that must hold for the step to pass. Used in test assertions.

failure_error_code.description: Error code emitted when this step fails. Cross-reference root error_codes[].

flows.description: End-to-end scenario paths. Multiple flows per feature (happy_path / fallback / deviation). Distinct from validation_sequence: flows are scenario-level paths; validation_sequence is a single API's fine-grained rule chain.

type.description: happy_path = primary success path; fallback = degraded / error-recovery path; deviation = alternate valid path (lazy creation, dual-read, etc.)

trigger.description: Precondition or event that activates this flow

outcome.description: Expected end state after all steps complete. Used directly in test assertions.

error_codes.description: Root-level error code catalog for this RFC. Contributing source (C) — prd_context is authoritative (A) for business error classification. Use these for cross-story dedup and for aligning scenario assertions.

body.description: Representative response body shape for this error

message.description: Human-readable description: when this error occurs and what triggers it

is_retriable.description: True = client should retry. Generates a retry-behaviour test scenario.

type.description: boundary = limit/overflow; race_condition = concurrent write conflict; timeout = downstream latency; concurrent = parallel request behaviour; idempotency = duplicate request handling

expected_behaviour.description: What the system must do in this case. Used directly in test assertion prose.

validation_step_ref.description: Step number from validation_sequence this edge case exercises. Null if cross-cutting.

inferred.description: True = edge case was inferred by the extractor, not explicitly stated in the RFC. Treat assertions as provisional.

cross_service_dependencies.description: Downstream services called by this feature. is_critical drives stub/mock prioritisation in test setup.

protocol.description: Communication protocol: REST, gRPC, Kafka, event, DB-direct, etc.

call_order.description: Relative call order in the happy-path sequence (0 = event-driven, no fixed order)

is_critical.description: True = failure of this dependency causes the feature to fail end-to-end. Generates a dependency-failure scenario.

failure_behaviour.description: How the feature behaves when this dependency is unavailable or slow

feature_flags.description: Feature flags that gate or alter behaviour. Each flag generates a flag_on and flag_off test scenario pair.

kill_switch.description: True = this flag can shut the feature off entirely. Generates a kill-switch scenario.

gated_behavior.description: One-line summary of what system behaviour this flag controls

rollout.description: Rollout strategy description, e.g. '5%->10%->50%->100% gradual with per-merchant rollback'

non_functional_requirements.description: Non-functional requirements in two layers: nfr_statements[] captures everything verbatim from the RFC (qualitative + quantitative); performance_targets[] is the structured subset extracted only when numbers are unambiguous. sdet-plan-generator reads both — statements for qualitative NFRs, targets for load scenario parameters.

nfr_statements.description: Verbatim NFR text from the RFC, one string per requirement. Always populated by the extractor — cheap, no parsing errors, preserves qualitative NFRs (data integrity, rollout strategy, cluster isolation) that cannot be meaningfully structured. sdet-plan-generator reads these for scenario intent; performance_targets[] provides the parsed numbers.

performance_targets.description: Structured subset of NFRs where the extractor can confidently parse numbers. Filled only for quantitative NFRs (throughput, latency, concurrency ceilings, time-based SLOs). Left empty when all NFRs are qualitative — nfr_statements[] is the fallback.

items.description: Only fields extractable from an RFC document. Test configuration decisions (load_test_type, ramp_up, duration, error rate threshold) belong in sdet_plan, not here.

description.description: Raw NFR statement as written in the RFC, e.g. '~4.5M+ wallet write ops/day; 500-1000 TPS per shard'

api_or_operation.description: Endpoint or named operation this target applies to, e.g. 'POST /wallets/balance-update'. Null when the target applies to the system as a whole.

throughput_tps.description: Target throughput in transactions per second, if stated in the RFC.

throughput_ops_per_day.description: Target daily operation volume, if stated in the RFC, e.g. 4500000.

latency_target_ms.description: Stated latency target in milliseconds, e.g. 200 for '<200ms'. Null if not specified.

latency_percentile.description: Percentile the latency target applies to, e.g. 'p99', 'p95'. Null if the RFC does not specify a percentile (treat as p99 by convention).

slo_deadline.description: Time-based SLO written in the RFC, e.g. 'must complete before 01:15 WIB', 'daily at 04:00 WIB'. Generates a deadline-breach scenario in sdet_plan.

concurrency_ceiling.description: Per-entity concurrency ceiling explicitly stated in the RFC. Generates two scenarios: (1) at safe_tps — assert 0% failure; (2) at degraded_onset_tps — assert failures are within documented bounds.

entity.description: Domain entity the ceiling applies to, e.g. 'wallet', 'booking', 'merchant_account'

safe_tps.description: TPS below which the RFC guarantees 0% failure.

degraded_onset_tps.description: TPS at which failures begin, per the RFC. Null if not stated.

security_compliance.description: Security and compliance requirements that generate explicit test scenarios: data masking, auth enforcement, PCI-DSS, GDPR, etc.

type.description: Compliance category. PCI-DSS / data_masking = card data must not appear in responses or logs.

reliability_targets.description: Timeout, retry, circuit-breaker, and availability targets. Generates timeout-behaviour and retry-exhaustion scenarios.

context.description: What this target applies to, e.g. 'IRIS async callback', 'balance update', 'cutoff worker SLO'

timeout_ms.description: Hard timeout for this operation in milliseconds. Generates a slow-downstream scenario: inject latency above timeout_ms and assert correct timeout behaviour.

retry_count.description: Max retry attempts on failure. Generates a retry-exhaustion scenario: downstream fails N+1 times → assert final error is surfaced correctly.

retry_policy.description: Retry timing strategy, e.g. 'exponential backoff 1s/2s/4s', 'linear 1s'. Informs retry-storm load scenario.

circuit_breaker.description: Circuit-breaker strategy description, e.g. 'opens after 50% error rate over 10s window, half-open after 30s'.

circuit_breaker_error_rate_pct.description: Structured error rate % at which the circuit breaker opens (e.g. 50.0). Used to configure the circuit-breaker activation load scenario: sustain errors above this threshold and assert circuit opens + fallback activates.

risk_areas.description: Risk areas identified in or derived from the RFC. P0 risks must have test coverage before any merge. Drives scenario priority in sdet_plan.

priority.description: P0 = blocking (test must exist before merge); P1 = required; P2 = recommended; P3 = nice-to-have

mitigation.description: How the RFC/implementation mitigates this risk — informs test assertion targets

extraction_gaps.description: Fields or sections the extractor could not fully resolve. Blocking gaps must prevent scenario generation for the affected area. SKILL must report extraction_gaps where blocking=true and halt generation for those scenarios.

field.description: JSON path of the missing/ambiguous field, e.g. contracts.rest[*].responses, status

detail.description: Full explanation of what is missing and why

blocking.description: True = do not generate test scenarios for the affected area until this gap is resolved. SKILL must surface these as blockers in sdet_plan.

open_questions.description: Unresolved design or implementation questions from the RFC. SKILL should surface these in sdet_plan as precondition gaps or deferred scenarios.

team_ownership.description: Teams involved in this RFC. Used for BrowserStack project routing (a PRD can span multiple RFCs across teams) and for dependency escalation paths.

owns.description: What system, service, or module this team owns within this RFC scope

browserstack_project.description: BrowserStack project slug for E2E test routing. Null if not applicable to this team's scope.
